title: Washboard players and the Brickley street band
summary: David Lewis, the Brickley brothers and Johnny Hill played washboard and jug on the street for tips; Punch hopes to play again.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Well, no. There was a special fella on there. Did you know- You ever heard of David Lewis? He was a good watchboard player.
I heard of him, but I don't think he was a bass player. I get confused. He was a good watchboard player.
Yeah, he was a good one. Is he around here? No. He was in New York. He was going to Canada.
And where did he play? He played a watchboard and sing.
And then he could dance like that. He was not tapped there. He was a funny man. Yeah, I know.
Did he play much here in the city? Well, he liked you.

I did a good while. Then he got out for the boy. And Gene Brickley, we call him Black Baby. He had a brother named Bannister Brickley. They all got together. Five of them. Johnny Hill, Bannister Brickley. Gene Brickley. And he still all with me. He saw Lewis. And what all did they play?

No, Bannister played the tough bass. Oh, yeah. Gene Brickley. Black Baby played the... Washboard. Johnny played the... The Phoenix thing, like I was telling you about. And I was... The... The deal. Johnny Hill, what's the name for? Oh, yeah. Juice out. Oh, yeah. Juice out, yeah. And that sounded good too, partner.
Would they hold on for a whole night in one place?
Yeah, they could, but I didn't get the job. They should go out and pick up money on the street.
Oh, I see. I got the picture now. Oh, yeah. Where would they go?

Well, I tell you. Yeah. They would go to Tormannous and go out to Spanish Ford. And places like that, you know. But they didn't, they never, they go around, you know, these dance halls or nothing. They wouldn't let them get there. But they'd go in there places and come back with money. No, no.
Why don't you take your cap off now, will you please, partner? Oh, no, no, Michael, how are you? Well... And, uh, let's see. What else do you want to talk about?

Well, the only thing I don't know now is... I still can't play, I'd like to give them a little chance at launching a horn around there. But, kind of slow, but I think it'll happen. Yeah. I think it'll happen. I got it deep in my mind that it's gonna happen. Well... Some guy gonna call me one time, and I'm gonna surprise him, and... There you go.
